importance_ranking.reason: Structural form variation is extreme — conical, hypar, barrel vault, shade sail, and modular umbrella are visually non-interchangeable. Buyers scan listing images to identify the structural form and aesthetic before reading any text; wrong form is an immediate skip.

Fabric material (PVC vs PVDF vs PTFE) drives 3–5x price variation and non-interchangeable durability tiers; structure type and shape are primary shortlisting gates. Buyers discover and compare across fabric grades during search — specs are a discovery signal, not merely a confirmation signal.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant fabricator brand with buyer recall — market is fragmented across regional fabricators; European fabric brands (Ferrari, Mehler, Sattler) are material brands, not structure brands that buyers search by name.
importance_ranking.reason: Custom-engineered, site-installed, multi-month project with long structural lifecycle. Fabricator track record, past project portfolio, installation team capability, and geographic service reach are primary vendor selection criteria equal in weight to specifications.

Per sq ft rate is a budget entry point and India price sensitivity is real, but final price is always custom-quoted per site dimensions and spec tier. Price comparison is only meaningful after fabric material and structural form equivalence is confirmed.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Modular tensile umbrella units are quoted per piece; large stadium or airport projects are quoted as lump-sum turnkey contracts. Per sq ft is dominant for car parking and commercial shade canopy — the primary segment — but unit must be shown to prevent price misreading across sub-segments.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per piece vs lump sum creates real price comparison confusion across sub-segments. A buyer comparing per sq ft listings against a per piece modular umbrella listing will fundamentally misread the price without unit clarity.

top_configurator_specs.reason: PVC Coated vs PVDF Coated vs PTFE Fabric represents a 3–5x price delta and non-interchangeable durability tiers (10-year vs 20-year vs 30+ year design life) — the single most price-determinative configurator in this category.

Conical, hypar, barrel vault, and dome forms require fundamentally different engineering, cable layouts, and fabrication methods — non-interchangeable across site geometry and aesthetic brief, with significant cost variation between forms.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Institutional, stadium, airport, and government buyers specify fire-rated fabric compliance (DIN 4102 B1, BS 476, ASTM E-126) as a mandatory procurement requirement — absent from the spec list despite being cited in market context as a standard fabric compliance dimension.

Institutional and government project buyers specify minimum design life (10/15/20/30 years) as a procurement criterion — directly tied to fabric material grade and a primary differentiator between PVC standard, PVDF, and PTFE tiers.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Application context (car parking, swimming pool, sports court, restaurant) routes the RFQ to sellers with relevant project experience and allows them to confirm structural feasibility and compliance requirements for that use case.

Structural form (conical, arch, cantilever, pyramidical) is non-interchangeable — sellers need this to assess fabrication feasibility, engineering requirements, and provide an accurate quote for the buyer's specific aesthetic and site geometry.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Fabric material (PVC vs PVDF vs PTFE) is the single most price-determinative input — sellers cannot provide an accurate quote or confirm product tier fit without knowing the buyer's fabric preference or budget tier.

buyer_spec_audit.image_upload_reason: Tensile membrane structure buyers frequently have a site photo, architectural sketch, or reference image of a structure they want to replicate — the structural form, site geometry, column placement, and aesthetic brief are extremely difficult to communicate through text spec values alone. An uploaded reference image allows sellers to assess structural feasibility, propose the correct form, and provide an accurate per-sq-ft quote without multiple back-and-forth exchanges.
